title: Sorting: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
oneLiner: The one move at the heart of merge sort: given two already-sorted lists, weave them into one sorted list in a single pass.
keyTakeaway: Merging two sorted arrays is O(n + m) -- one pointer into each array, always take the smaller of the two front values. Merge sort is exactly this merge step applied repeatedly to halves: log n levels of splitting, O(n) work to merge at each level, which is where its O(n log n) comes from.
explanation: Given two arrays that are ALREADY sorted, you never need to look backward to merge them: keep one pointer into each array, compare the two values they're pointing at, append the smaller one to the result, and advance only that pointer. Once one array runs out, everything remaining in the other is guaranteed to belong at the end (it's already sorted, and every value already appended is <= everything left), so just copy the rest over. This single merge is the building block merge sort is named after: split an array in half recursively down to single elements (trivially "sorted"), then merge pairs back together on the way up. Watch out for the two cleanup loops at the end -- forgetting to copy the leftover tail of whichever array didn't run out first is the most common bug here.
